newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins little changed, trend unclear.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins little changed, trend unclear.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds were little changed in thin trading on Friday in a market which has fallen into a summer lull, dealers said.
They gave mixed opinions as to where prices which rose strongly on Wednesday would go in the next few days as the market is not expecting any major events.
Bonds opened slightly higher as Russia followed a rise in other emerging markets on Ecuador's international credit rating, but the gains were killed by profit-taking later, dealers said.
"We opened a bit higher on the Ecuador rating, but later there was some selling interest," an ICFI-Moscow Partners dealer said.
On Thursday Moody's assigned Ecuador's long-term foreign currency debt at B1, the same level as Argentina and Brazil.
The dealer said he expected bonds to rise in the next few days.
"Russia is still cheap, you can still buy it," he said.

But a Moscow Narodny Bank dealer said the market was overheated after a strong rise on Wednesday following U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments, which investors took to rule out a rise in U.S. interest rates in the near future.
"At these levels I should expect profit-taking -- we have climbed too high," he said.
